title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (chapter V, 'Algèbre des figures', 1986): a set-theoretic 'figure' F in a set L (or X) is a family of subsets with the following data and properties.
- Its support is |F| = ∪_{A∈F} A.
- The 'interior' of A ∈ F is A° = A \ ∪{A' ∈ F : A' ⊊ A}.
- The interiors A° partition |F|, and each A is the union of the A'° for A' ⊂ A, A' ∈ F.
- So F is the face poset of a cell-like decomposition. The 'F-closed' subsets of |F| are the unions of elements of F, which are the down-sets for the Alexandrov topology.

Page 19 announces the definitions of 'F is a refinement of G' and 'F is a subdivision of G'. This page states and proves a Proposition giving two equivalent formulations.

(a) The first condition has two parts:
- For every A ∈ F, the set G^A = {B ∈ G : A ⊂ B} has a least element φ(A). This gives a monotone map φ: F → G.
- For A ∈ F and B ∈ G, the set A ∩ B is F-closed in |F|.

(b) The second condition also has two parts:
- For every A ∈ F there is a B ∈ G with A° ⊂ B°. This B is unique by disjointness of interiors; call it φ(A).
- The resulting φ is monotone.

Proof of a) ⇒ b):
- Let x ∈ A° and let B' ⊂ B = φ(A) with x ∈ B'.
- B' ∩ A is F-closed, so some A' ∈ F satisfies x ∈ A' ⊂ B' ∩ A.
- Since x ∈ A°, we get A' = A, hence A ⊂ B'.
- Minimality of B in G^A then gives B' = B. Hence x ∈ B°.

Proof of b) ⇒ a) (begun here, finished on p. 21):
- A = ∪_{A'⊂A} A'°, and A'° ⊂ φ(A')° ⊂ φ(A) by monotonicity. So A ⊂ φ(A).
- Minimality: if A ⊂ B', then A° ⊂ B° ∩ B' ≠ ∅, so B ⊂ B'.
- The F-closedness of A ∩ B is where Grothendieck pauses. He believes he needs the extra condition 'A° ⊂ B ⇒ A ⊂ B' (Corollary b′ on p. 21, and the marginal 'Lemme' on this page).
- He also reformulates it as: |F| ⊂ |G|, and the partition of |F| into F-interiors refines the partition induced by G.

Purpose: a combinatorial notion of refinement/subdivision of stratified 'figures'. It belongs to a set-theoretic foundation for the tame-topology / 'figures' programme of the 1980s, cf. Esquisse.
errors: The hypothesis A° ≠ ∅ for elements of a figure is used tacitly in the minimality step (p. 21) and is not stated on this page.

The 'complement' Grothendieck thinks he must add to b) (A° ⊂ B ⇒ A ⊂ B) seems derivable from b) as stated, given that G is itself a figure and interiors are nonempty. If C° ⊂ B, then C° ⊂ φ(C)°, so φ(C)° meets the G-closed set B. A point of φ(C)° lying in some D ⊂ B forces φ(C) ⊂ D ⊂ B. Since C ⊂ φ(C), this gives C ⊂ B. So the adjustment to the statement may be unnecessary. This depends on the exact definition of figure on earlier pages.
Several false starts are crossed out; no substantive error in the parts actually proved.

ideas.what: Figures as families of subsets with interiors A° partitioning the support (face posets of cell/stratum decompositions); F-closed sets = unions of elements
ideas.modern_name: face posets of regular cell complexes / stratifications; Alexandrov topology on posets
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures but not this formalism

ideas.what: Characterisation of when one figure refines/subdivides another via a monotone 'carrier' map φ: F → G with A° ⊂ φ(A)°, equivalently φ(A) = the least element of G containing A
ideas.modern_name: carrier map of a subdivision of cell complexes / refinement of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL/combinatorial topology (carrier of a subdivision)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary combinatorics of face posets and subdivisions. It is standard material written in Grothendieck's own 'figures' language, with no new result or connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 should read roughly: 'pour tout A ∈ F, B ∈ G, A∩B est F-fermé dans |F|' (A∩B, not A∩F).
'b) Pour tout A ∈ F, ∃ B ∈ G telle que A°⊂B° (B étant évidemment unique =: φ(A)), l'application φ: F→G ainsi obtenue est croissante' — the struck-out fragments are false starts.
In the a)⇒b) proof: 'il faut prouver que B'∈G, B'⊂B et x∈B' ⇒ B'=B' (the transcription's B'∉B is a struck-through ⊂).
Bottom margin reads roughly: 'Lemme N.7(?) b) Si A∈F, B∈G, A°⊂B, alors A⊂B'.
